headline: High: ctx can read filesystem/MCP context while RD-Agent broad-network egress creates leakage and cascading-action risk in default research workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse/Stop events and uses filesystem/MCP surfaces, while RD-Agent ingests papers/logs and runs browsers. If RD-Agent content is routed into ctx or vice versa, attacker-controlled text can be treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance isolation, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF RD-Agent outputs are copied into ctx-managed files or MCP messages
IF ctx parses browser or log content from RD-Agent as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all cross-agent text before handoff
Restrict ctx to allowlisted command templates only
Disable automatic ingestion of RD-Agent logs into ctx
Review one sample handoff for instruction-like content
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches harness records, graph data, and audit/runtime logs via filesystem/MCP, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, datasets, and secrets and sends data to external APIs. If they share a workspace or logs, sensitive material can flow from one agent into the other's outputs or third-party calls. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is inferred and escalated conservatively.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace or log directory
IF RD-Agent processes files containing financial reports or secrets in a shared path
mitigations: Separate workspaces and log directories per agent
Remove secrets from any shared folder before execution
Set API keys only in per-agent environment scopes
Inspect one shared directory for sensitive files
requires-engineering: enforce OS-level isolation between the agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and ctx can write filesystem state while RD-Agent writes logs and uses networked APIs. Overlapping mutable surfaces create a realistic conflict if they operate on the same directory or shared artifacts. Because no locking or shared-path guarantee is documented, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path
IF either agent mutates shared git or log state without a lock
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Run only one writer per shared repo at a time
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Check for concurrent writes before starting
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is designed to observe tool events and manage context, while RD-Agent is a research agent that can emit analyses and then call external APIs. If ctx forwards RD-Agent outputs as authoritative context, downstream actions can be taken on unverified claims. That creates a default-pathway risk of incorrect or harmful automation, especially because RD-Agent has broad egress.
conditions: IF ctx treats RD-Agent summaries as authoritative without verification
IF RD-Agent outputs are used to trigger browser or API actions
mitigations: Require human review before any external action
Insert a verification step between RD-Agent and ctx
Limit RD-Agent outputs to drafts only
Log source provenance on every forwarded claim
requires-engineering: add policy gates for action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports, competition datasets, and secrets while using third-party APIs; ctx touches audit/runtime logs and harness records. If the pair is used on regulated or confidential data, retention and residency obligations can diverge across the external APIs and logs. The profiles do not specify a DPA or residency guarantee, so the compliance risk is real but not fully pinned down.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through RD-Agent's external APIs
IF ctx logs contain confidential or personal data retained beyond policy
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent
Exclude regulated records from external API calls
Shorten log retention to the minimum needed
Verify vendor DPAs and residency settings
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
